title: Catalyst Module Manifest Schema
description: JSON schema for validating module.yaml files in Catalyst framework modules.

id.description: Unique module identifier, lowercase and hyphen-separated.

description.description: One-line summary of the process domain.

grounding_type.description: The kernel entity the module's artifacts ground to (for example `rule`).

kernel_version.description: The kernel versions the module works with, as a version specifier (for example `>=0.42.0`, `>=0.52,<1.0`). A release's manifest states it as `kernelVersion`; without it, the kernel that packages the release is assumed. Enforced: `catalyst init` and `catalyst sync` refuse a kernel outside it, and `catalyst check` reports a deployment outside it.

format.description: `3` for a module that declares its types in this file (§3.3); absent, the v2 layout of §2. The kernel reads both until 1.0.

namespace.description: The module's own meta-rule and invariant namespace (`SE`): its meta-rules are `rr-<NS>-NNN`, its invariants `INV-<NS>-n` (ADR-019). Composition widens and signs them like `rr-META-`.

aliases.description: Old ID → the ID it is now (`rr-META-009: rr-SE-001`). An old ID, short or widened and signed, keeps resolving: `validate` and `view` take it as the rule it now is, and `catalyst why <old>` explains the new one.

artifact.description: The entity type the tier opens, or `none`.

commit.description: For a tier with no artifact: the commit-subject prefix that marks it, e.g. `chore:`.

tiers.description: The module's ceremony tiers (`rr-META-006`), each `id`, `artifact` (the entity type the tier opens, or `none` when it needs no artifact, only its journal entry) and, for a tier with no artifact, `commit` (the commit-subject prefix that marks it, e.g. `chore:`). Every `--tier` and journal entry is checked against them, and `catalyst trace` accepts as ID-less only commits with a no-artifact tier's prefix. Without it: `chore` (no artifact, `chore:`), `fix` and `feature`.

entities.description: Format 3: the module's types, by ID prefix, each declared in this file (§3.3): its name, folder, fields, states, guards, `due`, `created_by`, sections and definition. Required unless the module lists `entity_types`.

schema.description: Path to ETD schema file relative to module root.

entity_types.description: The module's ETD files (`id`, `schema`). Format 2; required unless the module declares `entities` (format 3).

name.description: Slash command name without leading slash; its text is the module's CODE-OF-CONDUCT §4 entry.

spec_path.description: Deprecated (0.49.0, unused): agents get the command from the composed CODE-OF-CONDUCT §4.

commands.description: Slash commands the module adds (`name`, `description`, `argument_hint`); the command's text is its `code-of-conduct.module.md` §4 entry. `spec_path` is optional and unused.

entity_type.description: Entity type prefix matching an entity_types entry.

template_path.description: Path to markdown template relative to module root.

entity_type.description: Entity type prefix, or another module concept the definition covers.

path.description: Path to DEFINITION-<TYPE>-vN.md relative to module root.

required_paths.description: Paths every deployment must carry (`path`, optional `invariant`, optional `seed` template); checked by `scripts/check_deployment.py`.

path.description: Path relative to the working-copy root.

invariant.description: Invariant that requires it (e.g. one in the module's INVARIANTS.module.md).

seed.description: Module template used to create it when missing.

contributions.description: Content composed into a deployment (§6): `rules_of_rules`, `code_of_conduct`, `invariants`, `migrations` (`taskfile` is deprecated and ignored).

rules_of_rules.description: Module meta-rules appended to the deployed Rules-of-Rules.md (§6.1).

code_of_conduct.description: Module document types and commands inserted into CODE-OF-CONDUCT §3/§4 (§6.2).

invariants.description: Module invariants read with the kernel INVARIANTS.md (§6.4).

taskfile.description: Deprecated, ignored since kernel 0.70.0 (§6.5): a module ships no task; the criterion's Taskfile.common.yml has one task per command of the composed §4. Still accepted, as older module manifests carry it.

migrations.description: Folder holding the module's migrations and migrations.md index (§6.6).

spec_path.description: Path to skill definition SKILL.md file relative to module root.
